doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: The Depression and his father and grandfather in printing
summary: His father sold apples in the Depression; Bauer recounts the family's printing trade and how his grandfather learned on the job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Can I take you back just a few years — you were a teenager during the depression?
Well I was just about — what year was the depression?
‘38 or something like that? I don’t think I was a teenager. I remember my father, he went out selling apples for a nickel a piece. That’s how he had to make enough. Because it got so bad.
Did he lose his job during that time?

No, no he didn’t lose — I guess he did lose his job because that’s all he was doing. See he wound up to be — the whole family was printers outside of me. So his father wanted him to be a printer, and he became a printer. But then his father was older with his father’s brother, it was an uncle I guess of mine, but I didn’t know him very much, but they were old-time. And my grandfather couldn’t get along with his brother. And they had a fight. So that means my father and him were out. So my grandfather, he didn’t have no business then. And he went to work for a newspaper, I think it was the Bronx Home or North Side News, which eventually became the Bronx Home News. And don’t forget, my father went to the ninth — I went to the ninth grade elementary school, I quit. My father went to sixth grade and he quit. My grandfather went to the first grade. One year and he quit and he went to work. And you know what he wound up to be? A proofreader in a newspaper. Well you know why because you learn on the job. I tell these stories because that’s why I try to tell them, that’s what I did with music you know. See because he said you know like what makes Sammy run, I think there was a story like that, you know, like he just worked around the newspaper, picked up all the trash, and all of a sudden, well that’s what my grandfather did, but he did learn how to print because you see them setting type and then you learn, you didn’t even know you were learning how to read and write. Well that’s the best way to learn.
